summary: Daniel (Greek) 12 (13 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. Starting with '“At that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people. There will be a time of trouble, such as never was since there', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows faithfulness lived out in second temple period. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

questions.question: What is happening in Daniel (Greek) 12?
questions.answer: In 13 verses, this chapter daniel (greek) 12 (13 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. starting with '“at that time michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people. there will be a time of trouble, such as never was since there', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope. The setting is second temple period, written to jewish community. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Daniel (Greek) and why 12 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally anonymous / tradition, addressed to jewish community around intertestamental. This chapter fits the book's purpose as jewish literature — its themes of faithfulness, wisdom build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'righteousness' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Being in right standing, doing what is right. In this chapter, it appears in context of faithfulness. For a first-time reader: think of it as being in right standing, doing what is right, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through faithfulness and wisdom, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 7 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it will...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about faithfulness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
